subject: CloudHealth: Subprocessor custody & temporal scoping Q&A
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cloudhealth.com>
Cc: security@cloudhealth.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Custody windows & temporal scoping for subprocessors (follow-up)

Hi Lena,

Thanks again for the SIG-lite you shared earlier. As we're mapping dependencies for procurement and SOC 2 scoping, we have a couple of specific asks around custody and time-bounded access for subprocessors that came up in our internal review. Can you confirm the following for any subprocessor that touches runtime keys, telemetry, or raw logs?

- Custody boundary: which providers (and their internal teams) have long-term possession of keys or plaintext logs vs ephemeral access only?
- Temporal scoping: typical duration of access (minutes/hours/days), and whether access is session-limited (ephemeral keys) or persistent for troubleshooting windows.
- Log retention & exportability: canonical retention durations for raw telemetry and whether you can produce a time-bounded slice (e.g., 7-day window) per request.
- KMS residency: which regions/locations are keys resident in; is BYOK or HSM-supported?

If easier, a single CSV manifest and a short diagram called "key-custody-diagram.svg" would help our reviewer. We're aiming to bundle artifacts into a single packet for our procurement/sig review by EOD next week.

Appreciate it — cc'ing our infra reviewer (karthik) and procurement lead (ben) for timelines.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Trust & Risk
Redwood Inference

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cloudhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: CloudHealth Security <security@cloudhealth.com>, procurement@cloudhealth.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Custody windows & temporal scoping for subprocessors (follow-up)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the clear asks — attaching a compact manifest and a SIG-lite excerpt that should address most items. Quick answers inline below and the attachments include per-subprocessor rows for custody and retention windows.

- Custody boundary: Most telemetry and aggregated metrics are handled by our observability partner (Observix) with read-only dashboards; raw traces are accessible only to our infra on-call team and to Observix for 24 hours by default. For sensitive flows (payment tokens, PHI-transformed fields) Observix processes are configured in a restricted mode (no plaintext retained).
- Temporal scoping: standard ephemeral access for third parties is 1 hour for live debugging; when we escalate to a support snapshot we create a time-limited export (configurable up to 30 days) and deliver via secure share.
- Log retention: system logs 90 days by default; telemetry summaries 365 days. We can export a 7-day timeframe on request — see attached telemetry-export-20261203.csv sample.
- KMS residency: primary keys are in us-west-2; we support BYOK via KMS import and have an HSM-backed option for enterprise plans.

Attachments: CloudHealth_subprocessors_manifest.csv, CloudHealth_SIG-lite.pdf, telemetry-export-20261203.csv

Let me know if you want a short live walk-through of the manifest — happy to set 30 minutes.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Trust & Compliance
CloudHealth Solutions

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@cloudhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Custody windows & temporal scoping for subprocessors (follow-up)

Lena,

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying follow-ups from our security review team:

1) For Observix and any other telemetry processors, can you confirm whether they ever receive unredacted PII/PHI or whether fields are pseudonymized before export? If pseudonymized, is the mapping reversible by CloudHealth or only by the data owner?

2) For ephemeral debugging sessions (1 hour): are those sessions logged (who granted access, session-id, justification) and is there an audit trail export we can ingest into our SIEM? If so, please include the audit schema or a sample export.

3) For the HSM option: what SLAs/backups exist if a key is rotated/evicted? We need to understand recovery and proof that key material doesn't leave HSM boundary.

4) Finally, can you provide a short attestation (one paragraph) describing the maximum temporal window you will grant a vendor for active access to decrypted telemetry for our contract? We will include that text verbatim in our procurement addendum.

Artifact ask: if you can add a key-custody-diagram.svg (even a simple swimlane) and a one-paragraph attestation as a signed pdf, that would complete our packet. If attachments are large, please share a Drive link.

Cc'ing karthik/ben/jordan who will intake the artifacts and confirm acceptance criteria. Rough internal target: artifact receipt by Friday (2026-12-04) so procurement can close next week.

Thanks,
Naomi

Hi all,

Per our commitments, I've uploaded the requested artifacts to the Drive link below and included a short signed attestation PDF. Files uploaded: CloudHealth_subprocessors_manifest.csv, CloudHealth_SIG-lite.pdf, key-custody-diagram.svg, telemetry-export-20261203.csv, CloudHealth_attestation_signed.pdf.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cexample
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/Envelope/ABC123example
JIRA: RFI-4123 (internal tracking)

Attestation excerpt: "CloudHealth confirms that third-party vendor access to decrypted telemetry is time-limited and granted only for explicit debugging sessions; the maximum active access window granted to a third-party vendor without separate procurement approval is 30 days for exported snapshots, and 1 hour for live ephemeral sessions unless extended by documented escalation with justification."

If this meets your needs, please confirm so procurement can close the addendum. Happy to do a 20-minute call if you want to walk the artifacts.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Trust & Compliance
CloudHealth Solutions
